images.caption: The Confederation Bridge (French: Pont de la Confédération) spans the Abegweit Passage of Northumberland Strait. It links Prince Edward Island with mainland New Brunswick, Canada. Before its official naming, Prince Edward Islanders often referred to the bridge as the "Fixed Link". Construction took place from October 1993 to May 1997[2] and cost C$1.3 billion. The 12.9-kilometre (8 mi) bridge opened on May 31, 1997.[3] en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Confederation_Bridge

images.caption: Built between 1960-64, the Confederation Centre of the Arts is an arts centre containing a theatre, an art gallery, and a library.  Although the Confederation Centre of the Arts was built as a national memorial to the Fathers of Confederation who met at the Charlottetown Conference, the Centre is not itself dedicated to the Conference or to Confederation in general.  Instead, the art gallery has a permanent collection of Canadian art and also has exhibit space for traveling shows, while the theatre hosts traveling Broadway musicals and the annual "Anne of Green Gables - The Musical."

images.caption:
I left very early in the morning as I wanted to be at Prince Edward Island around sunrise. My objective was to get pictures of all the lighthouses on the island - the journey begins. Hope you like lighthouses as I believe I managed to get 49 of them out of 50, one was on the backside of a island so unavailable. This was a four day journey but worth while for me.
The Confederation Bridge crosses the Northumberland Strait from New Brunswick to Prince Edward Island. Before its official naming, Prince Edward Islanders often referred to the bridge as the "Fixed Link". Construction took place from October 1993 to May 1997 and cost $1.3 billion Canadian. The 12.9-kilometre (8 mi) bridge opened on May 31, 1997.
